scope: Evaluate whether the current HSConfig workflow stays slim and autonomous for any valid deck by allowing technically load-safe packages to proceed even when guide evidence is thin, mechanics are warning-only, option identity is unresolved, or claims are report-only, while still surfacing the first missing source-to-runtime link for follow-up.
source_backed_findings: The active operator contract states that HSConfig must produce a load-safe initial HearthRanger CustomConfig package for every valid deck input, with technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE, runtime_load_safe=true, and runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply defining the normal apply promise.

The operator contract deliberately separates minimal load-safe runtime apply from richer package usefulness: GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json are the required runtime files, while per-card CardID files, Combo.json, and identity-gated option rows improve usefulness but their absence alone must not block a package that remains technically valid.
The operator contract treats SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG as source confidence, not as the runtime-write gate, and explicitly says READY_TO_APPLY_WITH_WARNINGS still means the package is usable.

The apply gate implementation allows a package when operator_summary.json reports technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE and the required runtime structure is present; it records semantic_status and semantic_blocker_count as reasons, but does not use them as blockers.

The apply gate still hard-blocks true load-safety defects: missing operator summary, missing input manifest, missing CustomConfig or deck runtime directory, missing GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, normal-path Presume.json or Concede.json, nested runtime files, undeclared runtime files, stale summary entries, invalid runtime JSON, and technical_status values other than VALID_PACKAGE.

The no-block failure-mode summary groups technical_hard_block separately from source_depth_warning, warning_only_mechanic, future_mechanic_drift, guide_strength_gap, combo_uncertainty, and runtime_evidence_only_tuning; when runtime_apply_allowed is true and mode is load_safe_apply, non-technical categories produce load_safe_apply_allowed_with_warnings rather than a blocker.

The source claim lifecycle marks quarantined, report-only, unsupported, unknown, and unknown-future-mechanic claims as non-runtime candidates; runtime_claims_for_surface skips quarantined and report-only rows instead of blocking the package.

The source contract policy matrix is diagnostic-only at the operator gate. It classifies archetype, tech_slot, and replacement_option as report_only; globalvalue_numeric_tuning as runtime_evidence_required; discover_choice and choose_one_choice as conditional CardID claims that require exact option identity.

The surface gate requires explicit runtime-lowerable claim kinds per surface. Mulligan rows require mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard, GlobalValues runtime evidence claims are rejected with requires_runtime_evidence, and CardID claims are rejected when their claim kind or runtime confidence is not lowerable.
The mechanic registry defaults warning-only or unknown mechanics to report-only lowering policies with no default runtime block, and mechanic visibility summaries are explicitly non_blocking.

The operator documentation names choose_one as identity_gated_direct and generic board_position, generic_spell_target, location_activation, secret_timing, and generated_entity_random_pool as warning_only; unresolved or warning-only mechanics must be visible in warning_boundaries without blocking load_safe_apply.

The source claim gap report records card-level first_missing_link, source_depth_lane, recommended next claim kind, priority, and next source action; its first_missing_chain provides a single first follow-up item when source-to-runtime coverage is incomplete.

The source-to-runtime explainability report is diagnostic_only, always has apply_blocking=false, and projects claim and card rows into emitted_runtime_files, not_emitted_runtime_files, first_missing_link, why_not_emitted, and next_source_action.

Regression tests cover the core no-block contract: valid Wild decks produce VALID_PACKAGE and load_safe_apply; unknown semantic qualifiers remain warning-only; quarantined conflicting claims do not block; future/report-only/runtime-evidence claims do not block; warning-bearing future-mechanic packages stay load-safe.

Regression tests also protect the no-second-gate boundary by asserting that source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, and contract_spine_rows are not consumed by apply_gate, runtime_apply, or apply command paths.
repo_implications: Keep the architecture as a two-lane model: technical load safety decides normal runtime apply, while source quality and semantic completeness decide diagnostic richness and next-source work.
Do not add SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG, guide-depth closure, source-to-runtime explainability, mechanic completeness, option-identity closure, or config_usefulness as a second apply gate.

Continue emitting the minimal load-safe package for a valid deck even when only GlobalValues.json and Mulligan.json are authoritative enough for runtime apply; richer CardID and Combo output should be produced when evidence supports it, not required as a universal write precondition.

Keep warning-only mechanics report-visible through mechanic_visibility_summary, mechanic_drift_summary, warning_boundaries, and no_block_failure_mode_summary rather than mapping them to speculative VisionAI rows.

Keep unresolved Discover, Choose One, generated entity, hero-power transform, and similar identity-dependent behavior strict: exact option or transformed identity may lower, unresolved identity stays suppressed or report-only.
Keep globalvalue_numeric_tuning separate from guide-backed posture: numeric tuning remains visible but blocked until runtime evidence, while the package itself can still be load-safe.
Use source_claim_gap_report and source_to_runtime_explainability as the operator's first missing source-to-runtime link surfaces, but preserve their diagnostic-only status.

Keep hard blocks narrowly technical: unsupported filenames or blocks, invalid JSON, missing required runtime files, stale or forged package summaries, undeclared runtime files, nested runtime files, and normal-path legacy/diagnostic surfaces.

Preserve the existing regression pattern where every new warning or suppression category gets one test showing it remains visible and non-blocking, plus one test showing unsafe runtime shape still blocks.
Treat future mechanic support as a registry-and-test extension only after an exact documented VisionAI surface and deterministic lowering rule exist.
correctness_risks: If a warning-only mechanic is accidentally given a default runtime block, HSConfig can create a false runtime claim and may make the bot prefer an action the source contract cannot justify.
If unresolved option identity is guessed, Discover, Choose One, generated entity, Titan-like ability choice, or hero-power-transform behavior can be lowered to the wrong CardID or option row.
If report-only or low-confidence source claims are allowed into runtime_claims_for_surface, thin guide wording could silently become runtime authority.

If SOURCE_BACKED_STRONG or config_usefulness becomes an apply gate, technically valid packages with safe baseline output could be blocked for source-depth reasons that the current contract says are warnings.

If technical hard blocks are weakened to preserve no-block autonomy, malformed JSON, unsupported VisionAI blocks, missing required runtime files, stale summaries, or non-normal surfaces could be written to runtime.
If first_missing_link is computed from the wrong lane order, the operator may chase a lower-value source gap before the first missing runtime-safety or runtime-lowering explanation.

If start-of-game or deckbuilding effects are conflated with opening-hand mulligan intent, HSConfig can reintroduce the class of error where an effect enabler is held in Mulligan.json without explicit hand-required evidence.
If diagnostic reports start feeding apply paths directly, source-contract reporting could become a hidden second authority instead of an explanation layer.
slimness_risks: Adding a separate gate for every diagnostic report would bloat the operator model and contradict the current single apply authority.
Encoding every unsupported or future mechanic as executable behavior would turn the registry into speculative game-AI logic rather than a lean documented-surface mapper.
Duplicating warning-to-blocker classification across apply_gate, operator_summary, source_contract_audit, source_to_runtime_explainability, and mechanic_support would increase drift risk.
Making source-to-runtime explainability repair or mutate package output would overload a diagnostic report and blur ownership with the builders and routers.
Trying to solve all thin-source cases by adding generated fallback claims would expand the source model while reducing auditability.
Expanding normal output to Presume.json, Concede.json, or other optional surfaces without a separate design would widen HSConfig beyond its pre-run load-safe package scope.
Adding live-client, replay, winrate, or post-game tuning proof to HSConfig would duplicate HSTuner responsibilities and make any-deck pre-run generation heavier than necessary.
autonomy_risks: The system remains autonomous for producing a valid load-safe package, but warning-only mechanics, report-only claims, unresolved option identity, and runtime-evidence-only numeric tuning still limit how rich that package can be.
A deck can be load-safe but strategically thin when guide claims, exact mulligan evidence, exact combo sequences, or CardID-lowerable behavior are absent.

Autonomy depends on the builder continuing to emit safe baseline runtime files even when source evidence is incomplete; if baseline emission regresses, source warnings could become practical blockers.
Unknown future cards or mechanics can be made visible, but they cannot be autonomously converted into correct runtime behavior until a documented surface and deterministic lowering rule are added.

The current proof supports the no-block contract through local docs, implementation gates, and representative tests, but the claim that every possible valid current or future Hearthstone deck is covered is a contract-level and matrix-backed claim, not an exhaustive live-client proof. [uncertain]
If operators read READY_TO_APPLY_WITH_WARNINGS as gameplay optimization proof, the workflow can create false confidence even though it only proves load-safe package generation.
recommended_design_position: Keep HSConfig slim by preserving the current two-lane no-block contract. Lane one is technical load safety: package structure, required runtime files, supported filenames and blocks, valid JSON, input manifest, output-summary consistency, and absence of normal-path legacy surfaces decide whether hsconfig apply may write. Lane two is source and semantic richness: thin source evidence, report-only claims, warning-only mechanics, unresolved option identity, runtime-evidence-only numeric tuning, combo uncertainty, and first missing source-to-runtime links stay visible in reports and suppress only unsafe rows. Do not create a second apply gate from diagnostics. The next improvement should be to keep first_missing_link reporting precise and to extend mechanic or option lowering only when exact source identity and documented VisionAI surface authority are present.
